clauses.reason: The sole operative paragraph amends Executive Order 12187 so that section 1-101 sets the base production control level for marginal properties for the months January to March 1980, section 1-102 defines marginal properties by reference to the crude oil pricing regulations, and section 1-103 lets the Secretary of Energy conform those regulations; the order has no sunset or effective-date wording of its own. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 orders that the listed Executive Orders, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and lists the number 12209 in the No. column of its revocation table (offset 26806 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt). This is an express revocation that names this order. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the first-end date is its signing date, 1986-02-25; that is a reading of the text, not express wording, and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and filing date 1986-02-26 are not effective dates. Earlier candidates that do not name EO 12209 (the period of section 1-101 ending 1980-03-31, EO 12287 of 1981-01-28, the believed 1981-09-30 lapse of the statutory authority) are disclosed but not adopted, because none names this order or is shown to have extinguished its sections.

research_rationale:
EO 12209 (signed 1980-04-16; 45 FR 26311) was read in full in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12209.txt. It is a single amending paragraph that restates sections 1-101 to 1-103 of Executive Order 12187. The dossier evidence ACT:EO:12209>EO:12553 (an agent-located, independently reviewed provision) was re-read against the held EO 12553 text, whose revocation table lists the number 12209. The LOOKUPS number-citation search of the held order texts finds no order other than EO 12553 that names EO 12209. The machine searches (U.S. Code 0 hits, eCFR 0 hits, Federal Register catalog 2 hits that are EO 12553 and EO 12919) were read: EO 12919 only amends EO 11790 and does not name EO 12209. EO 12287 (1981-01-28), read in the held Federal Register text, decontrols crude oil and petroleum products without naming EO 12187 or EO 12209. Under the owner rulings of 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments) and 2026-10-28 (an endpoint needs a reason), the end is the instrument that names this order, EO 12553, and the unnamed candidates are disclosed. Original not yet confirmed as an authenticated official copy; the held text is the machine text layer of the official Federal Register PDF.

(2) Executive Order 12287 exempts all crude oil and refined petroleum products from the price and allocation controls but names neither EO 12187 nor EO 12209 and its section 3 authorizes entitlements actions for periods prior to it, so it does not extinguish this order. savings.reason: The order converted old oil from marginal oil wells to new oil status effective April 1, 1980 and fixed the base production control level for January to March 1980; those pricing consequences for past periods are accrued effects. EO 12287 section 3 itself contemplates actions for periods prior to its date. The order creates no continuing duty after revocation, and no held source shows an independent command that survives.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1980-03-31: last day of the months covered by restated section 1-101, before the order was signed on 1980-04-16; a period limit on one section, not shown to end sections 1-102 and 1-103 or the order.
source_notes.reason: Restated section 1-101 prescribes the base production control level for the months January, February and March 1980 only; disclosed as an earlier candidate end under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments.
